This leads to a probabilistic model where individual scores are deviations from a population mean P, following a normal distribution. The assumption of normality allows for statistical inference and predictive modeling. The concept of filial regression extends this to inheritance patterns, suggesting that offspring artistic scores regress toward the population mean, mirroring hereditary laws observed in stature and eye color. These primitives enable GSI to build Bayesian models for trait prediction and GSE to simulate evolutionary dynamics of artistic capability. Failure modes include non-normal distributions or non-linear inheritance, which would invalidate the core assumptions underlying these mappings.
